_review_notes.scope: AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) -- all figures below matched current sources and were NOT changed in value, only in structure.
changes_made: Restructured from prose-key/string-value format ('More than Rs 50 lakhs...': '10%') to numeric min_income/max_income/rate_percentage, matching final_tax_act.json's slab format, since both feed the same tax-computation logic
Added marginal_relief block -- was completely absent from the original file, and surcharge without it silently overcharges anyone just above a threshold
still_missing_not_fabricated: Exact marginal relief WORKED EXAMPLES / edge-case formulas for AOP, Firm, Company categories -- only the individual/HUF principle is captured below. Verify before use for non-individual filers.

individuals_huf._note_new_regime: Caps at 25% above 2 crore -- the 37% top slab does not exist under the new regime.

special_capital_gains_and_dividends.description: Dividend income and capital gains under sections 111A, 112, 112A
special_capital_gains_and_dividends.applies_to: both old and new regime; caps the surcharge attributable to THIS income specifically, not necessarily the taxpayer's entire surcharge rate

marginal_relief.principle: Surcharge cannot push total tax (incl. surcharge) on income just above a threshold higher than: [tax at the threshold] + [the actual amount earned above the threshold]. Relief = (tax + surcharge computed normally) - (tax at threshold + excess income over threshold).

worked_example.scenario: Individual, old regime, total income Rs 51,00,000 (Rs 1,00,000 over the Rs 50L threshold)
worked_example.tax_without_relief_at_10pct_surcharge: surcharge pushes total above what a Rs 50L earner would pay, by more than the Rs 1,00,000 excess income itself
worked_example.relief_applied: caps the extra tax so it never exceeds the Rs 1,00,000 excess income
worked_example.source_figures: illustrative structure only -- exact rupee example not reproduced here; verify against current source before hardcoding into a calculator
